hypothesis: Pragmatic listener at depth 3 with perceptual isolation, graded semantics, and utterance extension costs. name: visually_grounded_pragmatic_listener
hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions by modeling a communicative speaker who reasons about a perceptually grounded literal listener, rather than an abstract semantics-only agent. Bottom-up visual distinctiveness biases literal attentional selection toward prominent referents; communicative speakers anticipate this perceptual bias when selecting referring expressions; and pragmatic listeners invert this visually grounded speaker. On uninformative prior trials without an informative word, listener choices track continuous visual distinctiveness directly.

name: communicative_payoff_speaker
hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions by modeling a speaker who chooses utterances to maximize expected communicative success under a bounded linear payoff, rather than logarithmic information surprisal. On a display containing an identical twin pair and a solitary singleton with an additional distinguishing feature, hearing a shared feature leads listeners to favor the twin pair over the singleton, because an intended singleton would have been named with its unique feature; this sharply reverses the predictions of the twin-contrast solitary oddity listener, which mistakenly favors the singleton as an odd-man-out. When no informative expression is heard, listener expectations reflect that speakers prefer to target referents whose features permit unambiguous communicative success over incommunicable duplicates.

name: exclusive_description_cost_speaker
hypothesis: Speakers in reference games actively avoid producing non-exclusive descriptions that are shared with visual competitors, incurring a cognitive production cost whenever they use an ambiguous referring expression instead of an exclusive identifying label. Pragmatic listeners invert this ambiguity-averse speaker, inferring that when an ambiguous expression is produced, the speaker lacked any exclusive alternative for the intended referent. On uninformative trials where no informative word is uttered, listener expectations reflect that speakers prefer to communicate about referents that possess an exclusive identifying description.

name: twin_contrast_feature_prior_listener
hypothesis: Twin-contrast solitary perceptual oddity listener with visual feature complexity prior. Listeners interpret referring expressions by integrating a solitary perceptual oddity heuristic with baseline visual feature complexity expectations, where an odd-one-out pop-out bias operates exclusively when a solitary singleton contrasts against an identical twin pair rather than majority triplets or clusters. On uninformative prior trials without an informative word, when visual displays lack twin contrast, listeners expect speakers to target richer, feature-laden exemplars with greater descriptive complexity; when an informative referring expression is heard, selective attention to semantic applicability directs choice among matching referents, preserving solitary oddity pop-out when contrasting with twins. ### Refinement details relative to twin_contrast_solitary_oddity_listener - **Single stated change**: Extended twin_contrast_solitary_oddity_listener by incorporating visual feature complexity weighting into the ungrounded prior over candidate referents, adopted from rsa_l2_singleton_feat_color_valence_l0. - **Why it should fit better**: In visual reference games where no informative expression is provided (prior trials), participants exhibit a pronounced visual and communicative preference for feature-rich objects over minimal, featureless objects. The source model predicted uniform choice on all prior displays lacking identical duplicates, underpredicting choices for complex objects and overpredicting choices for sparse items; weighting ungrounded expectations by feature complexity captures these descriptive complexity preferences across prior displays while preserving twin-contrast solitary oddity pop-out and literal semantic matching during utterance comprehension. - **Recursion depth**: Unchanged at depth 0 (`choice_probs` evaluates `L_heur` directly without recursive speaker simulation). - **Parameters added or removed**: Added parameter `w_feat` (prior Normal(0.0, 1.0)); retained parameter `beta_prior` (prior Normal(0.0, 2.0)), parameter `beta_utt` (prior Normal(0.0, 2.0)), and parameter `lapse` (prior Beta(1.0, 9.0)). - **Code differences**: In `PARAMS`, added `"w_feat": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0)`. In `choice_probs`, updated prior computation from `prior = softmax_prior(params["beta_prior"] * is_singleton)` to `prior = softmax_prior(params["beta_prior"] * is_singleton + params["w_feat"] * ctx.feature_count)`, incorporating feature count weighting into ungrounded prior choices while leaving `L_heur` unchanged.

name: twin_contrast_base_rate_listener
hypothesis: Attenuated solitary perceptual oddity listener with twin contrast and familiarization base rates. When no informative expression is heard, listeners choose candidate referents by joint solitary oddity pop-out and prior familiarization frequency; when an informative expression is heard, selective attention to semantic applicability attenuates oddity pop-out among matching referents while continuing to weight candidate referents by their familiarization base rates. ### Refinement details relative to twin_contrast_solitary_oddity_listener - **Single stated change**: Extended twin_contrast_solitary_oddity_listener by incorporating contextual familiarization base-rate weighting from base_rate_solitary_oddity_listener. - **Why it should fit better**: In reference games with prior exposure or familiarization phases (such as E5_baserate), listeners develop empirical base-rate expectations favoring objects encountered more frequently. hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions by modeling a communicative speaker who chooses intended referents according to their visual feature surprisal, expecting speakers to target objects possessing rare features that deviate from the context ensemble. On uninformative trials where no informative word is uttered, listener expectations directly favor objects possessing high feature surprisal over common or featureless alternatives. When an informative referring expression is produced, pragmatic listeners invert this speaker using Bayes' rule, integrating the feature surprisal prior with linguistic applicability.

name: attentional_crowding_listener
hypothesis: Listeners have capacity-limited visual attention that suffers from visual crowding when candidate referents share features with similar display competitors. Attentional capacity allocated to each referent decays with its visual crowd size, so that visually isolated singletons receive focused attentional gain while redundant items suffer attentional suppression. Pragmatic listeners invert a communicative speaker who anticipates this attentional crowding constraint, while choices on uninformative prior trials directly track uncrowded visual attention.

name: feature_uncertainty_listener
hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions under lexical feature uncertainty, recognizing that an uttered word might not deterministically pick out a single intended visual dimension. When an expression is heard, the listener assumes the speaker primarily intended the conventional feature but maintains uncertainty that the word refers to another contextual feature present in the visual scene, weighting candidate referents by their joint possession of the named and alternative contextual features. On uninformative prior trials where no informative word is uttered, listener expectations reflect that speakers prefer to communicate about referents with greater descriptive feature richness.

name: evaluative_referent_utility_listener

The speaker evaluates this endowment according to their stated evaluative attitude—seeking maximal endowment under positive framing ('favorite'), minimal endowment under negative framing ('least favorite'), and retaining a baseline default preference for endowed referents under neutral framing. Pragmatic listeners invert this evaluative speaker via Bayes' rule, integrating the referent utility prior with communicative informativeness.

name: fewest_features_listener
